quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matthew Prince and CFO Thomas Seifert: Q2 2026 revenue $696.1 million, up 36% year-over-year; the U.S. was 51% of revenue (up 41%), EMEA 27% (up 30%) and APAC 14% (up 32%); large customers contributed 73% of revenue, up from 71% a year earlier.

CFO Thomas Seifert: remaining performance obligations (RPO) of $2.732 billion, up 7% sequentially and 38% year-over-year; current RPO was 64% of total RPO and grew 35% year-over-year. CEO Matthew Prince: new customer bookings increased at the fastest rate in more than five years and new pipeline grew sequentially at its fastest pace in five years.
quarterly_data.figure: RPO $2.732 billion, up 38% year-over-year; current RPO up 35%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Thomas Seifert, guidance: Q3 2026 revenue $736 million-$737 million (up 31%), operating income $129 million-$130 million, diluted EPS $0.34; full year 2026 revenue $2,864 million-$2,870 million (up 32%), operating income $443 million-$445 million, diluted EPS $1.25-$1.26; approximately 374 million shares and a 20% effective tax rate; network CapEx expected at 14%-15% of revenue for full year 2026 (7% in Q2).
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 revenue $736 million-$737 million; FY2026 revenue $2,864 million-$2,870 million, up 32%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matthew Prince and CFO Thomas Seifert, customers: 4,698 customers paying more than $100,000 a year, up 27% (accelerating from 25% last quarter), with 282 added in the quarter and a record 986 net additions year-over-year, records in every large-customer tier from $100,000 to over $5 million; dollar-based net retention 120%, up 2% sequentially and 6% year-over-year; more than 80,000 paying customers added in the quarter for 74% year-over-year paying-customer growth; more than 7.4 million developers on the platform, nearly two million added in Q2 versus 1.5 million in all of 2025; sales productivity up year-over-year for the 10th consecutive quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: 4,698 large customers, up 27%; dollar-based net retention 120%; 7.4 million+ developers

quarterly_data.signal: CFO Thomas Seifert: Q2 gross margin 73.1%, up 30 basis points sequentially (the first sequential improvement in eight quarters, per the CEO) and down 320 basis points year-over-year as paid-versus-free traffic growth shifts network cost into cost of revenue, a trend showing signs of stabilizing; he expects gross margin to stabilize around the current level and total unit economics to expand in the second half; operating income $96.1 million, up 33%, a 13.8% margin; net income $107.8 million, $0.29 per diluted share; free cash flow $56.4 million, 8% of revenue, up 69%; $4.2 billion in cash, equivalents and available-for-sale securities; headcount 4,700; severance and other restructuring charges of $151 million in Q2 ($99 million paid) and up to $165 million for 2026 (up to $130 million cash), with 2026 free cash flow expectations unchanged excluding them.
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin 73.1%; operating income $96.1 million (13.8% margin); free cash flow $56.4 million

quarterly_data.signal: Management (the speaker is labelled Matthew Prince in the transcript): against the Investor Day goal of GAAP profitability by the end of 2028 at the latest, Cloudflare is 'pacing ahead of that very clearly'; without the restructuring charges the Q2 GAAP net loss would have been around $18 million.
quarterly_data.figure: GAAP net loss around $18 million excluding restructuring charges

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matthew Prince, Q2 wins (unnamed customers): a leading digital-native media company signed a five-year $31.8 million contract for application services and Zero Trust; a Fortune 1,000 technology company an 18-month $15.9 million contract for application services and Workers; a Global 2000 European technology company a three-year $11 million contract; a large U.S. federal agency a five-year $7.7 million contract for Magic Transit and Network Firewall; a rapidly growing generative AI company a one-year $7.5 million pool-of-funds contract for the developer platform (chosen for zero egress); a leading technology company a one-year $6 million pool-of-funds Workers contract for its AI agent capabilities; a Fortune 100 technology company a three-year $5.2 million SASE contract; an APAC technology company a one-year $4 million Workers pool-of-funds contract after an $8.7 million application services contract last quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: $31.8 million; $15.9 million; $11 million; $7.7 million; $7.5 million; $6 million; $5.2 million; $4 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matthew Prince: in Q2, for the first time, more than 50% of the traffic on Cloudflare's network was not human (management says it crossed in May, earlier than its 2027 forecasts), and requests from AI agents keep growing; management (labelled Thomas Seifert in the transcript), with the caveat that it has called it wrong before: if the current trends continue, it thinks non-human traffic will be as much as 1,000 times human traffic in five years; over 80% of the major AI companies are Cloudflare customers, and the CEO says the largest AI providers are all customers.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 50% non-human traffic; over 80% of major AI companies are customers

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matthew Prince: since the start of Q3 (Content Independence Day and Agents Week) Cloudflare unveiled building blocks for a two-sided agentic marketplace - Monetization Gateway (customers sell any resource behind Cloudflare: web page, API, dataset or MCP tool), Wallets (buyers pay autonomously through agents) and cloudflare.pay (agent-friendly identity and trust) - and open-sourced Cloudflare OS; he estimates Cloudflare handles about half a billion requests per second (not audited), of which 1% to 10% could be monetized by micro-transactions, requiring support for about 10 million and scaling to 100 million financial transactions per second; north of 20% of the Internet sits behind Cloudflare.
quarterly_data.figure: about half a billion requests per second (unaudited estimate); north of 20% of the Internet behind Cloudflare

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Matthew Prince: Workers has become a meaningful contributor to revenue (no product breakout) and is 'the perfect platform for building agents and agentic workloads'; code built on vibe-coding platforms such as Lovable, Replit and Base44 at Wix is often deployed to Cloudflare as the preferred target; SASE and Zero Trust gained share pretty significantly in the last six months. CFO Thomas Seifert: Workers products remain the fastest-growing act, followed by SASE (Act 2); the TAM has grown from $30 billion at the IPO to north of $300 billion, and the business model is shifting from ratable SaaS toward pool-of-funds, consumption and T-shirt-sized contracts, making quarter-to-quarter forecasting harder.

CEO Matthew Prince: Cloudflare does not want to get into the business of renting servers - selling commodity compute that lets an AI company use 'your balance sheet and your credit rating in order to buy servers' is not attractive business, and selling commodity hardware is 'bad business for us' - while the largest AI providers are all customers; by scheduling diverse traffic it can in some cases get 10 times as much utilization out of every CapEx dollar; he expects the share of revenue through partners to keep rising and 'wouldn't be surprised if it gets north of 50%, even maybe over 60%', with large systems integrators interested in implementing Cloudflare OS.
quarterly_data.figure: 10 times utilization per CapEx dollar in some cases; partner share possibly north of 50%
